summary:
Lima department and the metropolitan area stand under the national framework of Peru, and the national assessment carried by the parent record applies here. No separate departmental or municipal regime modifying that framework was identified in the sources.

Lima's Jorge Chávez international airport had installed signage reading "for all persons with female identity" and "male identity". The national norm approved by Congress on 2 April 2025 bars such "ambiguous" signage as well as trans people's use of facilities matching their gender identity, so the airport's inclusive signs fall directly within the national prohibition.

On 12 February 2023 Rubí Torres Silvano, a 31-year-old transgender sex worker, was abducted from jirón Chancay in central Lima by the "Los Gallegos" extortion gang and killed with roughly 30 gunshots. The killing is recorded by the TLGBI Rights Observatory.
tangentialFactors: Enforcement of the national bathroom rule in Lima's public facilities is expected to run through security staff demanding identity documents (DNI) based on their own judgment of whether a woman entering is trans, per the activist Gianna Camacho. That discretion, rather than any written procedure, is what a trans visitor is most likely to meet in transit and commercial spaces.
localsOnly: A 2012 study by Universidad Peruana Cayetano Heredia found that 70% of trans women in Lima and Callao work in sex work, a documented exposure factor for police and public violence.
outOfScopeNotes: No Lima-specific breakdown of hate-crime or rights-violation data was identified; the observatory figures available are national aggregates that do not separate the department. Whether the Jorge Chávez airport signage remains in place after the national norm took effect is not established in the sources.
